analysis: The trial executed successfully but reduced host validation macro HR@10 to 0.4312, versus the supplied 0.4900 cumulative-memory result and 0.5050 baseline. Per-category HR@10 was 0.470 Movies_and_TV, 0.455 Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.350 Electronics, and 0.450 CDs_and_Vinyl. Separating input and output embeddings therefore did not support the representation-conflict hypothesis in this configuration. Losing the regularization and shared learning signal of tied embeddings is a plausible explanation, but these results do not establish the cause. Training, checkpoint reload, and predictor execution completed successfully; no test metrics were provided.
code_summary: One ConvRec network and one selected checkpoint per category, with four-category inference routing. The network uses causal residual convolutions with dilations 1/2/4/8, two-head causal attention, gated cumulative-prefix memory, and layer normalization. The experimental change adds an independent output embedding table initialized as a copy of the input table; both train jointly. Input embeddings encode histories and memory, while output embeddings score all positive, negative, and inference candidates with a learned item bias. Training retains recency-weighted sampled softmax, 256 sampled negatives, AdamW, seed 42, and the environment-controlled 200-epoch default. The predictor reconstructs the same architecture and strictly loads both embedding tables. No ensemble or checkpoint averaging is used.
